endpoints.description: Assets, liabilities and equity as at a date. A point-in-time statement rather than a range, so it cannot be filtered the way profit and loss is. Same nested Rows shape and accounting-method dependence.

endpoints.name: Cash Flow

endpoints.description: Cash movement for a date range, split into operating, investing and financing. Distinct from profit and loss on an accrual basis: profit and cash differ by exactly the working-capital movements this report shows, which is why a profitable business can run out of money.

endpoints.name: Customer Balance

endpoints.description: Every transaction in journal form for a date range, showing both sides of each entry. The double-entry view, useful for auditing rather than reporting.

endpoints.name: Profit And Loss
endpoints.suffix: /reports/ProfitAndLoss?customer={Customer?}&qzurl={Quick Zoom URL?:true|false}&accounting_method={Accounting Method?:Cash|Accrual}&start_date={Start Date?:YYYY-MM-DD}&end_date={End Date?:YYYY-MM-DD}&date_macro={Date Macro?}&adjusted_gain_loss={Adjusted Gain Loss?:true|false}&class={Class?}&item={Item?}&sort_order={Sort Order?:ascend|descend}&summarize_column_by={Summarize Column By?}&department={Department?}&vendor={Vendor?}&
endpoints.description: The profit and loss statement for a date range, with income, cost of goods, expenses and net income. THE SHAPE APPLIES TO EVERY REPORT IN THIS CONNECTOR: QuickBooks returns a nested Rows structure of sections, header rows, data rows and summary rows -- not a flat row set -- with a separate Columns block naming what each cell means. It must be flattened before use, and the section a row sits in is what gives it meaning. Note also that ACCOUNTING METHOD is a parameter, not a property of the data: the same period returns different numbers on a cash basis than on an accrual basis, so the method has to be stated for a figure to mean anything.
